title: Odessa's life in Chicago and the divorce
summary: Odessa stayed in Chicago and finished high school while Jackson was on the road; they divorced about 1955 and he kept paying her rent.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: And Odessa -- Odessa was a wonderful woman. She was a wonderful woman, you know. I brought her from Tennessee and she was a very ambitious girl. She didn't go no further than the ninth grade down there in Memphis, and she started to living in Chicago. She liked to live in Chicago because she had relatives there, you see?
Uh-huh.

So I let her stay there and she went and finished high school there. She sent to Memphis and got her credits and she finished high school there and then she got to be a dentist's assistant, you know. And she worked at that and I used to send the money home just as regular even though I was never there.

And, really, the marriage didn't mean anything to her because I never was home and she didn't like to travel and she didn't like New York at all because she had no friends there, and the only friends that she had there was Tyree's wife and Dizzy's wife. Other than that she didn't know nobody. Her friends were all in Chicago.
Right.
And her family, her aunts and cousins and things. So I let her stay there. That was it. That's where she was at. So this went on like that clear till in the fifties, you know.

Uh-huh.
You were married when?
We was married Decoration Day in 1940.
Uh-huh.
That's right, on May the 30th.
Uh-huh.
And this went on like that until 1955, '56. And I went to her and I told her, 'Gee whiz. You're a good girl. I'm not doing justice to you. I'm not a husband to you. I'm never home,' you know?
Uh-huh.
And 'you should get somebody that's going to be around you all the time because you deserve this,' you know?
Uh-huh.
So 'you go get the divorce papers and I'll sign them,' which I did.
Uh-huh.
And I said, 'I'll tell you what I'll do. I'll pay the rent for you until you find you somebody.
I'll still pay the rent for the apartment." And I did.
That's beautiful.
Clear up to 1960 when I went to Europe.
Uh-huh. And I couldn't send the money any more.
